lesson_title: Written in Arabic, Spoken in Afrikaans
hook_text: Some of the earliest written Afrikaans was not written by Dutch settlers. It was written in Arabic script.
clip_script: At the Cape, enslaved people from Indonesia, India, Madagascar and Mozambique worked the vineyards and the kitchens. They could not marry legally or wear shoes. But they built communities. Exiles like Sheikh Yusuf and Tuan Guru brought Islam, and in 1794 the first mosque rose in Bo-Kaap. To talk to their owners and to each other, enslaved people spoke Dutch, and changed it, adding Malay and Khoe words like baie and kwagga. Later, Muslim teachers wrote that language down in Arabic letters. Afrikaans has many parents.
visual_style: A Bo-Kaap street with colourful houses and a minaret; a page of Arabic-script text transforms into Afrikaans words; vineyards in the background.
pacing: Measured, building to the reveal of the script.
